newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Worst S.African rand depreciation over-economist.
newsitem.headline: Worst S.African rand depreciation over-economist.

text.p: The worst of the rand's depreciation appears to be over and it is expected to settle close to 4.80 rand to the dollar by the end of 1997, Boland Bank economist Francois Jansen said.
In his latest economic review, written before this week's fresh tumble by the rand, Jansen said the rand was "completely undervalued".

Jansen said he believed that "the chances are very good that the adjustment process has come to an end and that the value of the rand will return more towards fundamental economic principles in future."
But he warned the part played by the ruling government in pursuit of a responsible economic policy carries equal weight.

"Yet we think that the worst is behind us and that the rand/dollar exchange rate will be close to 4.80 rand per dollar by the end of 1997." The rand closed firmer on Friday at 4.7290/7340, up from 4.7510/7560 on Thursday.
Jansen said that although speculators and negative market sentiment have helped determine the rand exchange rate, there had been good fundamental economic reasons for the sharp weakening of the rand.

These included the abolition of the financial rand which had protected the commercial rand, the lack of foreign capital inflows, a drop in gold and foreign exchange reserves, excess money supply, an economic slowdown and the fact that the rand had bee overvalued between July 1994 and January 1996.
